    About IIST

    The Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST) is a premier academic institution dedicated to the study and research of Space science and technology in India. It is located in Valiamala, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, and was established in 2007 to promote higher education and research in space sciences, technology, and engineering.

    Meet Our Vice Chancellor

    Prof. Dipankar Banerjee, Vice Chancellor, joined IIST on 14 October 2024. He is an astrophysicist with a bachelor’s degree in physics (St. Xavier’s college) and master’s degree in Theoretical Physics from University of Kolkata. He has obtained his PhD from Indian Institute of Astrophysics and completed two postdoctoral tenures in reputed institutions in Europe. He served as Director, Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES), Nainital from 2019-2024. He is also a senior professor at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.

    Dr Banerjee’s area of interest is the Sun and the solar atmosphere. His work involves theoretical and numerical modeling using data from ground and space-based instruments. His work has enriched our understanding of the Sun and its impact on Space Weather.

    The Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST) is a premier academic institution dedicated to the study and research. It is located in Valiamala, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, and was established in 2007 to promote higher education and research in space sciences, technology, and engineering.

    The institute seamlessly integrates research and development with academics. The major theme of IIST’s research portfolio is the application of cutting - edge science to generate new technologies and applications with a focus on space research. IIST houses many state-of-the-art facilities to bolster research in frontier areas of science and technology. 
    IIST has also been instrumental in exploring research collaborations and exchange of scientific ideas with international academic and research organizations. This includes international collaborations, both as Memorandum-of-Understanding (MOU) at the Institute-level as well as at an individual level of faculty-to-faculty collaboration.
    Research at IIST is curiosity-driven yet impact-oriented, fostering a culture of inquiry, creativity, and public service through vibrant PhD and post-doctoral programmes. In addition, many BTech and Masters students carry out their theses in the Institute helping them develop critical thinking, research skills, and innovation capacity early on.

    --

    IIST being under Dept. of Space, Govt. of India, has a close association and collaboration with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). This gives students and researchers collaborative access to the laboratories in ISRO and an opportunity to participate directly in ISRO's missions. Graduates from IIST can be absorbed by ISRO in various capacities, and the institution plays a significant role in preparing skilled personnel for India's space program. Currently 1442+ Alumni  of IIST are placed in ISRO

    --

    IIST is equipped with state-of-the-art laboratories, research centers, and facilities that support space-related research, including ground stations, simulation labs, and avionics laboratories. The campus is self-sufficient and houses students with all necessary administrative facilities such as canteens and kiosks, medical facility, a bank.

    --

    Many of IIST’s graduates go on to work with ISRO and other space organizations. The institution has a dedicated placement cell that helps students secure internships and full-time jobs in space-related fields. IIST's affiliation with ISRO also provides its students with unique career opportunities in India's space missions.

    --

Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST), situated at Thiruvananthapuram is a Deemed to be University under Section 3 of the UGC Act 1956. IIST functions as an autonomous body under the Department of Space, Government of India. The idea of such an institute was mooted keeping in mind the need for high quality manpower for the Indian Space Research Organization, one of world’s leading scientific organizations engaged in space research and space applications.

The Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology IIST is located in Thiruvananthapuram and functions as a Deemed to be University under Section 3 of the UGC Act 1956. It operates as an autonomous institution under the Department of Space Government of India. IIST was established to address the need for high quality scientific and technical manpower for the Indian Space Research Organization a global leader in space research and applications.
